title: Agent orchestration and multi-agent patterns
summary: Learn how a request can be classified by required action and authority, routed to a specialist, checked by an independent reviewer, and either assembled or returned for bounded revision.
description: This lesson preserves the complete workflow from human request through routing, specialist fanout, joined work output, independent review, approval, and final delivery. A rejected output returns to the router. Revision is bounded, and exhausted work is reported to the human instead of looping forever.
safetyNotice: This page performs no network, storage, deployment, or external code-execution actions. Its simulation compares supplied fixture strings in the browser. A displayed pass means only that those static fixture comparisons matched.
diagramLabel: Interactive agent-orchestration workflow with four specialist branches, a work-output join, independent review, approval, and a revision return to the router
textAlternativeLabel: Read the complete workflow as text
textAlternative: Human request goes to Router agent. Router agent classifies intent at Decision. Decision branches by required action and authority: build to Coder agent, review to Reviewer agent, investigate to Investigator agent, and operate to Operator agent. Every specialist branch joins at Work output. Work output goes to Independent reviewer. Approval goes to Assembled response and then Human receives result. Revision returns specifically to Router agent for reclassification and bounded repair. If the revision limit, permission boundary, or evidence budget is exhausted, the assembled response reports the unresolved state to the human rather than starting an endless loop.
practiceInstructions: Choose one response in each case. Each case is solvable from its supplied facts. Feedback and the worked solution remain hidden until that case has been attempted. Completion is earned only after all three cases have a correct answer.
takeaways: Classify a request by the action, authority, evidence, and acceptance criteria it requires, not by a verb in isolation.
Keep specialist production and completion authorization separate. Self-review or an invented test result cannot authorize completion.
Route rejected work back through the router while preserving the acceptance contract, permission boundary, evidence provenance, and remaining revision budget.
Stop bounded repair when its limit is exhausted and report the unresolved evidence and options to the human.
Model-family assignments can be illustrative configurations, but this lesson provides no current prices, benchmarks, capability rankings, vendor-exclusive assignments, or purchasing recommendations.

simulation.heading: Browser-only fixture simulation
simulation.description: Run deterministic string comparisons over the supplied initial output, repaired output, and exact expected output. This does not execute the pseudocode or call an external service.
simulation.failedLabel: Failed as expected: initial output differs from the expected fixture
simulation.passedLabel: Passed: repaired output exactly matches the expected fixture
simulation.executionDisclaimer: Result scope: local equality checks over embedded strings only. No external code, agent, test runner, file write, or deployment was executed.

nodes.label: Request
nodes.heading: Human request
nodes.description: The human supplies the complete CSV fixture, expected output, permission boundary, acceptance contract, and one-revision limit.

nodes.label: Route
nodes.heading: Router agent
nodes.description: The router derives the required action and authority. It preserves the acceptance criteria and records ambiguity, evidence needs, permissions, and the remaining repair budget.

nodes.label: Decide
nodes.heading: Intent decision
nodes.description: The decision has four retained branches: build, review, investigate, and operate. Classification depends on the requested effect and authority, not on verbs alone.

nodes.label: Build
nodes.heading: Coder agent
nodes.description: The coder may propose a bounded source change in the isolated task workspace. The coder cannot approve its own work or write to production.

nodes.label: Review
nodes.heading: Reviewer agent
nodes.description: The review route performs read-only analysis of a supplied artifact. It does not silently gain permission to edit or publish that artifact.

nodes.label: Investigate
nodes.heading: Investigator agent
nodes.description: The investigator explains evidence from supplied records and clearly separates observations from inferences. Investigation is read-only unless separate authority is granted.

nodes.label: Operate
nodes.heading: Operator agent
nodes.description: The operator route covers an authorized state-changing action. Missing permission requires clarification or escalation, not inferred authority.

nodes.label: Join
nodes.heading: Work output
nodes.description: Outputs from all four specialist branches join here. For the CSV task, the dossier includes the initial failure, bounded repair, exact fixtures, and provenance for every test record.

nodes.label: Check
nodes.heading: Independent reviewer
nodes.description: A reviewer separate from the producing coder checks the supplied patch, fixture equality, permission boundary, and acceptance contract. Independence assumes no shared hidden answer editing or coordinated fabrication.

nodes.label: Approve
nodes.heading: Assembled response
nodes.description: Approved evidence is assembled with the patch summary, exact fixture result, provenance, permission scope, and known limitations.

nodes.label: Receive
nodes.heading: Human receives result
nodes.description: The human receives either the approved result or a bounded unresolved report. No workflow state is represented as a real deployment or external action.

artifacts.label: Worked request
artifacts.title: Fictional CSV repair request
artifacts.body: Fix the report transformation so each line_total equals quantity multiplied by unit_price and the TOTAL row equals the sum of line_total. Return the corrected pseudocode and exact output for the supplied input. Do not access a network, production data, or files outside the isolated task workspace. One repair attempt is allowed after independent review.

artifacts.label: Complete input
artifacts.title: report.csv
artifacts.body:
item,quantity,unit_price
Notebook,2,3.50
Pen,3,1.20
Folder,1,4.25

artifacts.label: Exact expected output
artifacts.title: report.expected.csv
artifacts.body:
item,quantity,unit_price,line_total
Notebook,2,3.50,7.00
Pen,3,1.20,3.60
Folder,1,4.25,4.25
TOTAL,,,14.85

artifacts.label: Routing decision
artifacts.title: Required action and authority
artifacts.body: Primary route: build to Coder agent. Reason: the requested deliverable changes transformation pseudocode in an isolated workspace. Required authority: local task-workspace write only. Independent Reviewer remains the completion authority. Operator is not selected because no external system or shared file may be changed.

fields.label: Ambiguity
fields.value: None for the supplied fixture and expected output

fields.label: Revision budget
fields.value: One bounded repair after the initial review

fields.label: Escalation
fields.value: Ask the human if required data, authority, or evidence is missing

artifacts.label: Preserved contract
artifacts.title: Acceptance and permissions
artifacts.body:
A. Preserve the input header and all three source rows, and emit the output header shown in the expected fixture.
B. Compute each line_total as quantity × unit_price using decimal values.
C. Format monetary outputs with two decimal places.
D. Compute TOTAL from line_total values, expected 14.85.
E. Do not use network access, production data, external writes, or deployment.
F. Independent review must compare the actual supplied output with the exact expected fixture.
G. At most one repair is permitted; an unresolved second rejection is reported to the human.

artifacts.label: Illustrative configuration
artifacts.title: Concrete diversity without a ranking
artifacts.body: A router can use a heterogeneous candidate pool without assigning any vendor exclusively. For example, a fictional low-budget classification slot might be configured to evaluate candidates from Meta Llama, Mistral, Qwen, or Phi, while a fictional complex-drafting or separate-review slot might evaluate candidates from DeepSeek, NVIDIA Nemotron, Z.ai GLM, GPT, Claude, or Gemini. The slot labels are planning examples, not claims about current price, capability, availability, benchmark position, or suitability. Actual selection would require dated provider documentation, measured task evidence, applicable terms, and the operator's constraints. Explicit authority is still required for a higher-risk action regardless of which family is assigned.

artifacts.label: Four complete mini-records
artifacts.title: Classification follows effect and authority
artifacts.body:
BUILD
Fictional artifact identity: Preview.tsx, lesson revision P-17.
Request: “Add a read-only preview panel and return the source diff.”
Destination: ui/Preview.tsx in the isolated lesson workspace.
Authorization: edit only that destination; no network, shared-file, or deployment access.
Classification: Coder, because the required effect is a bounded source write.
Outcome record: proposed diff P-17-R1 created for independent review; no external publication claimed.

REVIEW
Fictional artifact identity: supplied diff P-17-R1 for Preview.tsx.
Request: “List violations of acceptance criteria A through D. Do not modify files.”
Destination: read-only review record REVIEW-P-17-R1, not the source file.
Authorization: read the supplied diff and criteria only; no edit or publication authority.
Classification: Reviewer, because the requested effect is evaluation rather than modification.
Outcome record: REVIEW-P-17-R1 records clause-by-clause findings and leaves completion pending for the independent fixture check.

INVESTIGATE
Fictional artifact identity: parser.log revision L-4 and report.csv fixture F-3.
Request: “Determine why source row 3 was skipped. Separate observed lines from hypotheses.”
Destination: investigation record INV-L4-F3.
Authorization: read L-4 and F-3 only; no configuration, file, or service changes.
Classification: Investigator, because the requested effect is evidence analysis.
Outcome record: INV-L4-F3 records the five-column expectation as observed evidence and a schema mismatch as an unconfirmed hypothesis.

OPERATE
Fictional artifact identity: approved report.csv revision REP-14.
Request: “Publish REP-14 to the shared reporting folder.”
Destination: fictional shared path /reports/approved/report.csv.
Authorization: fictional change authorization CHG-EXAMPLE-7, scoped only to REP-14 and that destination.
Classification: Operator, because the requested effect changes shared external state and requires explicit authorization.
Outcome record in this lesson: NOT EXECUTED. The static lesson records the intended receipt fields as artifact REP-14, destination, authorization identifier, timestamp, actor, and resulting checksum, but supplies no real receipt and makes no publication claim.

Verb check: “Review and correct the shared report” contains the word review, but correction is a write. The router must clarify the target and authority before choosing a write-capable route.

artifacts.label: Escalation rule
artifacts.title: Do not infer permission
artifacts.body: If a request says only “fix the report” and does not identify whether the learner wants advice, a local patch, or a write to a shared report, the router asks which effect is intended and what authority exists. Ambiguous wording is one possible failure mode. This lesson does not claim it is the most common failure mode.

artifacts.label: Initial specialist output
artifacts.title: Incorrect pseudocode, revision 0
artifacts.body:
rows = parse_csv(input)
emit_header("item", "quantity", "unit_price", "line_total")
total = decimal("0.00")
for row in rows:
  line_total = decimal(row.quantity) * decimal(row.unit_price)
  emit(row.item, row.quantity, format2(row.unit_price), format2(line_total))
  total = total + decimal(row.unit_price)  # defect: adds unit price
emit("TOTAL", "", "", format2(total))

artifacts.label: Bounded repair
artifacts.title: Patch and corrected pseudocode, revision 1
artifacts.body:
Patch:
  rows = parse_csv(input)
  emit_header("item", "quantity", "unit_price", "line_total")
  total = decimal("0.00")
  for row in rows:
    line_total = decimal(row.quantity) * decimal(row.unit_price)
    emit(row.item, row.quantity, format2(row.unit_price), format2(line_total))
-   total = total + decimal(row.unit_price)
+   total = total + line_total
  emit("TOTAL", "", "", format2(total))

Corrected pseudocode:
rows = parse_csv(input)
emit_header("item", "quantity", "unit_price", "line_total")
total = decimal("0.00")
for row in rows:
  line_total = decimal(row.quantity) * decimal(row.unit_price)
  emit(row.item, row.quantity, format2(row.unit_price), format2(line_total))
  total = total + line_total
emit("TOTAL", "", "", format2(total))

artifacts.label: Specialist log
artifacts.title: Bounded actions
artifacts.body:
Revision 0: drafted pseudocode and output from the supplied fixture. The defective accumulator added unit prices 3.50 + 1.20 + 4.25, producing 8.95.
Review result: rejected because TOTAL was 8.95, not 14.85.
Revision 1: changed only the accumulator expression, retained explicit header emission, and regenerated the supplied output.
Writes represented: lesson dossier text only.
External execution, network access, storage, publication, and deployment: not performed.

artifacts.label: Review route example
artifacts.title: Read-only acceptance check
artifacts.body:
Input artifact: fictional diff P-17-R1 changes total += unit_price to total += line_total.
Destination: read-only record REVIEW-P-17-R1.
Authorization: inspect the supplied diff and contract clauses B and D; do not edit it.
Outcome: the expression now sums computed line totals and is consistent with expected TOTAL 14.85 for the supplied fixture. Completion still depends on the independent fixture comparison.

artifacts.label: Role boundary
artifacts.title: Producer is not completion authority
artifacts.body: The specialist may explain what it changed, but its statement “tests pass” is not evidence unless a named, inspectable test record exists. The independent reviewer authorizes completion only from supplied evidence and the acceptance contract.

artifacts.label: Investigation route example
artifacts.title: Observed fact versus inference
artifacts.body:
Input artifacts: fictional report.csv fixture F-3 and parser.log revision L-4.
Destination: investigation record INV-L4-F3.
Input fixture row: Folder,1,4.25
Input log: line 4: skipped; reason=expected 5 columns, observed 3
Observed: the parser logged a five-column expectation and a three-column row.
Inference: the parser may have been configured for an output schema while reading an input schema. This inference would require configuration evidence before it could be confirmed.
Authorization: read F-3 and L-4 only; do not edit or operate any system.
Outcome: observation and hypothesis are recorded separately.

artifacts.label: Evidence provenance
artifacts.title: Where each fact came from
artifacts.body:
Input values and expected output: embedded fictional lesson fixtures.
Initial and repaired pseudocode: embedded worked records authored for this lesson.
Initial and repaired output comparisons: deterministic equality checks available in this page.
External runtime, production logs, vendor benchmarks, and deployment evidence: none supplied and none claimed.

artifacts.label: Operation route example
artifacts.title: Authorized external change
artifacts.body:
Fictional artifact identity: approved report.csv revision REP-14.
Requested effect: publish REP-14 to fictional shared path /reports/approved/report.csv.
Supplied authorization: fictional change record CHG-EXAMPLE-7, scoped to REP-14 and that destination.
Required receipt: artifact identity, destination, authorization identifier, timestamp, actor, and resulting checksum.
Outcome in this static lesson: NOT EXECUTED. No receipt, checksum, publication, or external change is claimed. If identity, destination, or authorization were absent or ambiguous, the operator would return a clarification record rather than infer permission.

artifacts.label: Permission boundary
artifacts.title: Allowed and prohibited effects
artifacts.body:
Allowed in the worked task: draft and inspect text in the lesson; compare embedded strings in the browser.
Not allowed: write a shared file, call an API, access credentials, deploy code, alter production, or claim that such an action occurred.

artifacts.label: Test record 1
artifacts.title: Initial implementation fails
artifacts.body:
Fixture: complete report.csv shown in this lesson.
Produced output:
item,quantity,unit_price,line_total
Notebook,2,3.50,7.00
Pen,3,1.20,3.60
Folder,1,4.25,4.25
TOTAL,,,8.95
Expected final row: TOTAL,,,14.85
Result: FAIL. The three row calculations match, but the defective accumulator adds unit prices: 3.50 + 1.20 + 4.25 = 8.95. The contract requires the sum of line totals: 7.00 + 3.60 + 4.25 = 14.85.

artifacts.label: Test record 2
artifacts.title: Repaired fixture comparison
artifacts.body:
Repaired supplied output:
item,quantity,unit_price,line_total
Notebook,2,3.50,7.00
Pen,3,1.20,3.60
Folder,1,4.25,4.25
TOTAL,,,14.85
Exact expected output: identical text shown in report.expected.csv.
Result when the browser comparison is run: repaired string equals expected string. This is a static fixture comparison, not external code execution.

artifacts.label: Revision ledger
artifacts.title: One allowed repair
artifacts.body:
Initial submission: rejected.
Preserved criteria: A through G unchanged.
Repair requested: replace the incorrect accumulator source with line_total; preserve explicit header emission; do not broaden permissions.
Repair used: 1 of 1.
Next rejection rule: no second repair. Return an unresolved report to the human with the failing record and options.

artifacts.label: Independent review record
artifacts.title: Acceptance decision
artifacts.body:
Producer: Coder role.
Reviewer: separate Independent Reviewer role.
Checks:
A. Output header and three source rows are present in the supplied repaired fixture.
B. Each supplied line_total is correct: 7.00, 3.60, 4.25.
C. Monetary fields use two decimal places.
D. Repaired TOTAL is 14.85 and the embedded repaired string matches the embedded expected string.
E. No external action is represented.
F. Evidence is the embedded input, output, patch, and static comparison.
G. One repair was consumed.
Decision for the supplied fictional fixture: approve the repaired fixture result. This authored record does not establish external execution or correctness on untested inputs.

artifacts.label: Review assumption
artifacts.title: What independence means here
artifacts.body: The workflow assumes the reviewer did not secretly edit the producer's answer, share a hidden answer key during production, or coordinate fabricated evidence. Role labels alone do not prove independence. A real deployment would need process controls, separate evidence access where appropriate, and auditable provenance.

artifacts.label: Stop condition
artifacts.title: No endless revision loop
artifacts.body: Return to Router only while a permitted repair remains and the requested repair stays inside the original contract. When the one-revision budget is exhausted, evidence is unavailable, or required authority is missing, route to a human report stating the blocker, preserved criteria, attempted work, and safe next options.

artifacts.label: Completed worked response
artifacts.title: Assembled result for the human
artifacts.body:
Status: approved for the supplied fictional fixture only.
Change: total now accumulates line_total rather than unit_price; output header emission remains explicit.
Exact output:
item,quantity,unit_price,line_total
Notebook,2,3.50,7.00
Pen,3,1.20,3.60
Folder,1,4.25,4.25
TOTAL,,,14.85
Evidence: embedded input, expected output, one-line accumulator patch, repaired output, and static fixture comparison.
Permissions represented: lesson-local text and browser string comparison only.
Revision budget: one repair used; none remains.

artifacts.label: Delivery
artifacts.title: What the human receives
artifacts.body: The response includes the route, corrected pseudocode, exact output, review basis, evidence provenance, used revision count, and limitations. It does not say a production file was changed or that an external test suite ran.

artifacts.label: Known limitations
artifacts.title: Scope not established by this fixture
artifacts.body: Only one three-row fixture is supplied. Empty files, malformed CSV, quoted commas, negative quantities, very large values, alternate decimal rules, and rounding beyond two decimal places are not tested. The pseudocode is illustrative and was not executed by this page. Production readiness, performance, security, and compatibility are UNKNOWN; establishing them would require an identified implementation, executable tests, runtime environment, and authorized review.

practiceGroups.title: Case 1: ambiguous action and missing permission
practiceGroups.prompt: Request: “Review the shared report and fix anything wrong.” Facts: no destination, file contents, write permission, or authorization are supplied. What should the router do first?
practiceGroups.solution: Ask whether the human wants read-only analysis or an authorized write, request the artifact or location needed for that scope, and obtain explicit authority before any state-changing route. The word “review” does not remove the write implied by “fix.”

practiceGroups.title: Case 2: self-review and invented tests
practiceGroups.prompt: A coder returns a patch and says, “I reviewed my own work and all 42 tests passed.” No test command, fixtures, output, or separate reviewer record is supplied. Can the workflow authorize completion?
practiceGroups.solution: No. Keep completion pending and obtain inspectable test evidence plus review by a separate completion authority. A self-authored pass statement and an unsupported test count do not establish execution or correctness.

practiceGroups.title: Case 3: rejected work and bounded rerouting
practiceGroups.prompt: Contract: total must be 14.85, external writes are prohibited, and one repair is allowed. Review rejects revision 0 because total is 8.95. Which route preserves the contract?
practiceGroups.solution: Return to the router with the unchanged acceptance contract, explicit failing record, prohibited external writes, and one remaining repair. Route the bounded accumulator fix to the coder. If that repair is rejected, report the unresolved result to the human instead of looping again.

choices.label: Ask for the intended effect, artifact, and explicit write authority before selecting a state-changing route.
choices.feedback: Correct. The request combines possible read-only analysis with a possible shared-state write. Clarification prevents the router from inventing permission.

choices.label: Send it directly to the Reviewer because the request begins with “Review.”
choices.feedback: Not correct. Classification by the first verb ignores the requested correction, which may require a write. The missing artifact and authority remain unresolved.

choices.label: Send it to the Operator and treat the request itself as write permission.
choices.feedback: Not correct. A vague request does not establish the target, scope, or authority for changing a shared report.

choices.label: Yes. The coder is closest to the implementation and can approve its own statement.
choices.feedback: Not correct. Proximity to the implementation does not supply independent completion authority, and the claimed tests have no inspectable provenance.

choices.label: No. Keep completion pending until inspectable evidence and a separate review decision are supplied.
choices.feedback: Correct. This preserves role separation and prevents a fabricated or unsupported test claim from authorizing completion.

choices.label: Yes, because 42 tests is enough evidence even without records.
choices.feedback: Not correct. A numerical claim without commands, fixtures, output, or provenance does not establish that any test ran.

choices.label: Return to the router with the failure, unchanged contract, permission boundary, and one remaining repair.
choices.feedback: Correct. The router can assign the narrow accumulator repair while preserving acceptance criteria and the finite revision budget.

choices.label: Let the coder upload the report to an external service to find the problem faster.
choices.feedback: Not correct. External writes are prohibited. Rejection does not expand authority or erase the original contract.

choices.label: Keep returning rejected work forever until some specialist marks it passed.
choices.feedback: Not correct. Endless retries discard the one-repair limit and create pressure to approve without evidence. Exhaustion must be reported to the human.
